crop: Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis), selected tenera seedlings, Cameroon

sheet.text: MINADER technical and economic sheet for an oil palm plantation (October 2024, published May 2025): 143 palms per ha in 9 m triangles; production starts about 3 years after planting; fresh fruit bunches 4, 6, 8 then 13 t/ha; oil 25% and kernels 10% of bunch weight; peak production from 7 to 25 years; economic life about 30 years; profitability in year 8; harvest every 7 to 10 days, processing within 48 hours; more than three quarters of the crop from December to May.

fertilizer.text: Twice a year in March and October. Young palms (1 to 3 years) about 1 kg per palm a year; years 4 to 6 about 1.5 kg; from year 7 about 2 kg, mainly potassium chloride and kieserite (S1).

budget.text: Seedlings 160 at 2,000 FCFA; clearing 20 and staking 30 person days at 2,500; holes 200 and planting 300 FCFA per palm; Mucuna cover 12 kg at 1,000; glyphosate 1 L a year at 6,500; circle weeding 100 FCFA per palm twice a year; pruning 100 per palm; weeding 40,000 and fertilizing 25,000 FCFA per ha a year; harvest 20,000 rising to 50,000 FCFA. Potassium chloride 600, kieserite 700, urea 600 FCFA/kg (S1). Rodent guards of galvanized mesh around young palms (S1).

yields.text: Smallholders in Cameroon produce under one tonne of palm oil per ha, a quarter of smallholders in Indonesia and Malaysia (S2).

prices.text: Village plantations: the price of a tonne fell from 105,000 to about 80,000 FCFA (June 2025); Socapalm adds an internal bonus of 65 FCFA/kg for its planters (S3).
